algorithm.Title: Mouth Ulcers - Male (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Male
Definition: Mouth ulcer assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.

questions.Question: Are fluid-filled blisters on or around the lips the main concern rather than ulcers inside the mouth?
questions.Information: The cold-sore family is not generated. Arrange in-person clinical assessment through the Qatar route approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED).

questions.Question: Has the ulcer lasted longer than 3 weeks, is it unusually large or near the throat, is it bleeding or becoming more painful and red, or are there ulcers elsewhere on the body with joint symptoms?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends arranging clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) or dentist for these features - prolonged ulcers can occasionally indicate a more serious condition.

questions.Question: Is this a typical, recent mouth ulcer with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance: mouth ulcers are common and should clear up on their own within 1-2 weeks.

advice.Title: Routine mouth ulcer follow-up
Content: Book a clinical or dental review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) for these features.
Call Back If: ulcer grows or bleeds more.

advice.Title: Governed care for a minor mouth ulcer
Content: Use a soft toothbrush, cool soft foods/fluids if swallowing safely, and avoid irritating spicy, salty, acidic, or rough foods. Mouthwash, analgesic gel/spray, steroid lozenge, and salt-rinse advice require exact age, pregnancy/breastfeeding, allergy, swallowing safety, medical conditions, and current-medicine checks under the approved Qatar pathway. Do not apply aspirin to the ulcer.
Call Back If: lasts longer than 3 weeks; becomes larger, more painful, recurrent, or associated with fever, dehydration, weight loss, eye/genital lesions, or immunocompromise.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What is the person's exact age and sex, are they pregnant or immunocompromised, how long has the lesion been present, and is there fever, dehydration, weight loss, trauma, tobacco/betel use, medicine exposure, eye/genital lesions, or safeguarding concern?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 09 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: How large is it, and is it painful?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 09 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Any ulcers elsewhere on the body or joint pain?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 09 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What has a safe parent or caregiver observed about alertness, breathing, pain, swelling, fever, eating or drinking, sleep, play, and normal activity?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Child assessment adds safe-caregiver observations without inventing a different clinical threshold.
